title: I'd really appreciate some support!
author: StandardModel
selftext:
[My Lil Weirdos](https://preview.redd.it/sautxkp9yhth1.png?width=1122&format=png&auto=webp&s=430716388a1105c5760af8f4aebd0aa0d8052ab1)

Hi, I’m CellsAfterHours, working on Cells: After Hours. These are Pip and Thump in an in-engine alpha shot. The game is a little microscopic world with characters, homes and a story, and this is a commercial project still in development.

The workflow uses Codex for the Godot code and AI image generation for artwork, with human-led design and story direction. One concrete piece of the asset work: the illustrated cast sits on enclosed 3D meshes. This build adds contour-color blending and face-readable turning, and prepares the six cast meshes at build time to reduce first-load work. Getting the illustrations to feel at home in a 3D scene takes more than generating another image.

I’d welcome a critical eye on the result. Do Pip and Thump feel like they belong in the same world as the surrounding structures? If you’ve brought AI illustrations into a 3D game, what helped keep the style consistent?

For anyone interested in supporting development, the current 0.9.0-rc1 alpha is available for Mac, Windows and Linux. It’s $19.99USD one time, including all future updates free. There’s no free demo. Screenshots and downloads: [https://payhip.com/b/LMCi7](https://payhip.com/b/LMCi7)
